title: Elevation Health Assessment Tool - Version 2.0
description: Healthcare Technology Evaluation Assessment with 61 questions across 4 categories

steps.title: Reimbursement
steps.description: Evaluate payor-based reimbursement strategies, data infrastructure, and regulatory requirements
steps.helpText: This section evaluates your company's approach to healthcare reimbursement, data strategy, and regulatory compliance for revenue generation.

q1_payor_reimbursement.title: Does your business model rely on collecting data for payor-based reimbursement?
q1_payor_reimbursement.subCategory: Annual Physician Fee Updates and Reimbursement Codes

Yes.rationale: Payor-based reimbursement indicates established revenue model with regulatory framework

No.rationale: Alternative revenue models can be equally viable - redirects evaluation focus

q1_payor_reimbursement.helpText: Payor-based reimbursement involves collecting and exchanging data with insurance providers for payment of healthcare services.

rolloverText.payor-based reimbursement: A revenue model where healthcare providers receive payment from insurance companies (Medicare, Medicaid, private insurers) based on services rendered and documented through specific data collection and reporting requirements.

q2_data_strategy.title: Do you have a written data strategy for exchanging data with any payers and is this written strategy updated regularly?

Yes.rationale: Documented data strategy demonstrates comprehensive planning and regulatory readiness

No.rationale: Lack of documented strategy creates significant operational and compliance risks

q2_data_strategy.helpText: Your reimbursement data strategy should cover data types, standards, and interoperability requirements needed to meet reimbursement requirements for both governmental and commercial payers.

rolloverText.data strategy: A comprehensive plan outlining how data will be collected, stored, processed, and exchanged with payers, including data standards, security measures, and compliance requirements.
rolloverText.updated regularly: Data strategies should be reviewed and updated annually at minimum to reflect changes in data and reimbursement policies.

q2_data_strategy_upload.title: Please upload your documented data strategy
q2_data_strategy_upload.helpText: Upload your comprehensive data strategy document covering payer data exchange requirements.

q3_successful_exchanges.title: Have you already been exchanging data with these payers for successful reimbursements?

Yes.rationale: Proven track record of successful payer data exchanges demonstrates operational readiness

No.rationale: No proven track record requires validation of strategy and implementation

q3_successful_exchanges.helpText: Successful data exchanges with payers demonstrate operational capability and reduce implementation risk.

rolloverText.successful reimbursements: Confirmed payments received from payers based on data submitted, indicating that data exchange processes are working correctly and meeting payer requirements.

q4_data_infrastructure.title: Does your data infrastructure support your reimbursement strategy (i.e., currently active exchange or readiness to exchange data) with at least 5 top insurers in the US?

Yes.rationale: Infrastructure supporting major insurers demonstrates scalability and market readiness

No.rationale: Limited infrastructure coverage may restrict market penetration and growth

q4_data_infrastructure.helpText: You must move beyond manual or point-to-point data exchange toward API-based models to meet demand and regulations. Consider regulatory optimization beyond just compliance.

rolloverText.data infrastructure: The technical systems, APIs, databases, and networks that enable secure collection, storage, processing, and exchange of healthcare data with payers.
rolloverText.top 5 insurers: Major insurance providers like UnitedHealth, Anthem, Aetna, Cigna, and Humana that represent significant market coverage.

q4_infrastructure_upload.title: Please upload data infrastructure modeling or architecture documentation
q4_infrastructure_upload.helpText: Upload technical architecture diagrams, API documentation, or infrastructure maps showing payer connectivity.

q5_onc_certified_updates.title: If you are pulling or pushing data from ONC-certified health IT or EHRs for reimbursement, does your data strategy include updating your data models for pulling or pushing data from these sources?

Yes.rationale: Updated data models ensure compatibility with certified systems and regulatory compliance

No.rationale: Outdated data models create integration risks and compliance gaps

q5_onc_certified_updates.helpText: ONC-certified health IT systems have specific data model requirements that must be accommodated in your integration strategy.

rolloverText.ONC-certified health IT: Health information technology systems certified by the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology, ensuring they meet federal standards for interoperability and security.
rolloverText.data models: Structured representations of how data is organized, stored, and accessed within systems, including field definitions, relationships, and formats.

q6_regulatory_officer.title: Do you have personnel (such as a Chief Regulatory Officer) monitoring upcoming policy changes that could impact data strategy for reimbursement?

Yes.rationale: Dedicated regulatory oversight ensures proactive compliance and strategic adaptation

No.rationale: Lack of regulatory oversight creates significant compliance and strategic risks

q6_regulatory_officer.helpText: A Chief Regulatory Officer ensures full compliance, provides strategic direction, develops compliance plans, and stays ahead of regulatory changes.

rolloverText.Chief Regulatory Officer: Senior executive responsible for ensuring organizational compliance with laws and regulations, monitoring regulatory changes, and developing strategic responses to policy shifts.

q6_regulatory_officer_upload.title: Please upload resume or credentials of responsible regulatory personnel
q6_regulatory_officer_upload.helpText: Upload resume, job description, or credentials of personnel responsible for regulatory oversight.

uploaded.rationale: Personnel documentation validates regulatory oversight capabilities

q7_risk_mitigation.title: Do you have a documented risk mitigation data strategy (e.g., VBC shift, new data requirements, new data standards) for upcoming policy changes?

Yes.rationale: Documented risk mitigation demonstrates proactive planning and business maturity

No.rationale: Lack of risk mitigation planning creates vulnerability to policy changes

q7_risk_mitigation.helpText: Proactive risk management demonstrates business and data infrastructure maturity and planning sophistication.

rolloverText.VBC shift: Value-Based Care - a healthcare delivery model where providers are paid based on patient health outcomes rather than volume of services provided.
rolloverText.risk mitigation data strategy: Plans and procedures to address potential disruptions from regulatory changes, including backup systems, alternative data sources, and compliance adaptation measures.

q7_risk_mitigation_upload.title: Please upload risk mitigation plan documentation
q7_risk_mitigation_upload.helpText: Upload document describing risk mitigation plan for data handling for reasonably expected policy shifts.

uploaded.rationale: Risk mitigation documentation validates strategic planning

q8_chief_data_officer.title: Do you have personnel acting in the role of Chief Data Officer exploring the value, legality and pathways to leveraging the data you are already collecting?

Yes.rationale: Chief Data Officer ensures data quality, strategic leverage, and competitive advantage

No.rationale: Lack of data leadership limits strategic data utilization and revenue opportunities

q8_chief_data_officer.helpText: A Chief Data Officer ensures data quality and access, leads data monetization efforts, enhances decision-making, reduces project risks, and ensures regulatory compliance.

rolloverText.Chief Data Officer: Executive responsible for data governance, quality, and strategic utilization to increase revenue, enhance decision-making, create competitive advantages, and ensure compliance.
rolloverText.data reuse: Strategic utilization of collected data for multiple purposes beyond the original collection intent, including analytics, research, and revenue generation.

q8_cdo_upload.title: Please upload resume or credentials of Chief Data Officer
q8_cdo_upload.helpText: Upload resume, job description, or credentials of personnel responsible for data strategy and governance.

uploaded.rationale: CDO documentation validates data leadership capabilities

steps.title: FDA Regulatory
steps.description: Assess FDA approval requirements, clinical trials, and regulatory pathways
steps.helpText: This section evaluates FDA regulatory requirements for your product, including approval pathways and clinical trial needs.

q9_fda_required.title: Is a premarket review by the FDA required prior to marketing your product?

Yes.rationale: FDA requirement indicates medical device classification with established regulatory pathway

No.rationale: No FDA requirement reduces regulatory burden and time to market

q9_fda_required.helpText: Certain product types require FDA approval based on intended use, invasiveness, clinical purpose, medical image analysis, or claims of clinical outcome improvement.

rolloverText.premarket review: FDA evaluation process required before a medical device can be legally marketed in the United States, ensuring safety and effectiveness.
rolloverText.FDA required: Products intended for diagnosis, treatment, prevention of disease, or clinical decision-making may require FDA oversight.

q10_review_type.title: What type of review is required?

Premarket Approval (PMA).rationale: PMA pathway for high-risk devices with established regulatory framework

De Novo Review.rationale: De Novo pathway for novel devices with no predicate, showing innovation

510(k) Clearance.rationale: 510(k) pathway for moderate-risk devices with established predicate

Exempt from premarket notification.rationale: Exemption reduces regulatory burden while maintaining safety

I Don't Know.rationale: Regulatory uncertainty creates significant planning and compliance risks

q10_review_type.helpText: FDA regulatory pathways vary based on device risk classification and predicate device availability.

rolloverText.PMA: Premarket Approval - most stringent FDA review for high-risk (Class III) medical devices
rolloverText.De Novo: Regulatory pathway for novel devices with no existing predicate device
rolloverText.510(k): Premarket notification demonstrating substantial equivalence to existing device

q10_fda_pathway_upload.title: Please upload FDA pathway documentation or regulatory strategy
q10_fda_pathway_upload.helpText: Upload documentation supporting FDA pathway determination or regulatory strategy plan.

uploaded.rationale: FDA pathway documentation demonstrates regulatory planning

q11_approval_status.title: Has approval been obtained?
enum: No, the approval process has begun and the application has been submitted
No, the approval process has begun but the application has not been submitted
No, the process has not begun

Yes, it has been obtained.rationale: FDA approval obtained demonstrates regulatory compliance and market readiness

No, the approval process has begun and t.rationale: Application submitted shows progress but creates timeline uncertainty

No, the approval process has begun but t.rationale: Process begun but no submission creates significant timeline and approval risks

No, the process has not begun.rationale: No process initiation creates major regulatory and market entry risks

q11_approval_status.helpText: FDA approval status directly impacts market entry timeline and regulatory compliance.

q11_approval_upload.title: Please upload FDA approval letters or submission package documentation
q11_approval_upload.helpText: Upload FDA approval letters, clearance letters, or submission package cover letters.

q11_approval_status: No, the approval process has begun and the application has been submitted

uploaded.rationale: FDA approval documentation validates regulatory status

q12_clinical_trial_required.title: Is a clinical trial required to support market authorization of your product?

Yes.rationale: Clinical trial requirement understood with regulatory pathway clarity

No.rationale: No clinical trial required reduces development timeline and costs

I don't know.rationale: Clinical trial uncertainty creates significant development and regulatory risks

q12_clinical_trial_required.helpText: Clinical trials may be required based on device classification, risk level, and available predicate data.

rolloverText.clinical trial: Research study conducted with human participants to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a medical device or intervention.

q13_trial_status.title: Is the necessary clinical trial complete?
enum: No, the trial has not begun and/or I don't know where to begin to conduct a trial

Yes.rationale: Completed clinical trial provides evidence base for FDA submission

No, trial is currently underway.rationale: Ongoing trial shows progress but creates timeline uncertainty

No, the trial has not begun and/or I don.rationale: No trial initiation creates major development and approval risks

q13_trial_status.helpText: Clinical trial completion status directly impacts FDA submission timeline and approval probability.

q13_trial_upload.title: Please upload clinical trial documentation
q13_trial_upload.helpText: Upload documentation of completed or active clinical trial including study summary, aims, and results.

uploaded.rationale: Clinical trial documentation validates development progress

q14_data_management.title: Does clinical trial for FDA approval need further data collection or management assistance?
enum: No, trial data collection is sufficient and being managed confidently
No, trial is underway, but data management needs to be improved
I don't know where to begin to handle data collection and management for the trial I need to conduct

No, trial data collection is sufficient.rationale: Confident data management ensures trial integrity and regulatory compliance

No, trial is underway, but data manageme.rationale: Data management improvements needed but trial progressing

I don't know where to begin to handle da.rationale: Data management uncertainty creates significant trial execution and compliance risks

q14_data_management.helpText: Proper clinical trial data management is essential for FDA submission quality and regulatory compliance.

rolloverText.data management: Systematic collection, cleaning, validation, and analysis of clinical trial data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and regulatory compliance.
rolloverText.data warehousing: Centralized repository for storing, organizing, and managing large volumes of clinical trial data.

steps.title: Privacy & Data Protection
steps.description: Comprehensive assessment of HIPAA compliance, data governance, and privacy regulations
steps.helpText: This section evaluates your organization's compliance with healthcare privacy regulations, data governance frameworks, and patient rights.

q15_individual_data.title: Does your business/products collect individual data of any kind?

Yes.rationale: Data collection acknowledged - enables proper privacy assessment

No.rationale: No individual data collection reduces privacy compliance burden

q15_individual_data.helpText: Individual data includes PII, PHI, ePHI, and EHI - each with specific regulatory requirements for collection, storage, and sharing.

rolloverText.individual data: Any information that can identify a specific person, including personal, health, or electronic health information.
rolloverText.PII: Personally Identifiable Information - data that can identify a specific individual
rolloverText.PHI: Protected Health Information - health information that can be linked to an individual
rolloverText.ePHI: Electronic Protected Health Information - PHI stored or transmitted electronically
rolloverText.EHI: Electronic Health Information - broader category including all electronic health data

q16_hipaa_enforcement.title: Have you ever had a HIPAA enforcement action?

Yes.rationale: Previous enforcement action indicates compliance history requiring review

No.rationale: No enforcement history indicates good compliance track record

q16_hipaa_enforcement.helpText: HIPAA enforcement actions indicate compliance violations that may affect current assessment.

rolloverText.HIPAA enforcement action: Formal regulatory action taken by HHS Office for Civil Rights for violations of HIPAA privacy or security rules, including fines, corrective action plans, or monitoring agreements.

q17_remediation_status.title: Have all findings been addressed and remediated, with corrective action documented?

Yes - Enforcement action was dismissed.rationale: Dismissed enforcement action indicates resolved compliance issues

Yes - All deficiencies remediated.rationale: Full remediation shows commitment to compliance improvement

No - Remediation still in progress.rationale: Ongoing remediation indicates unresolved compliance risks

q17_remediation_status.helpText: Complete remediation of HIPAA violations demonstrates commitment to compliance and risk mitigation.

q18_privacy_policy.title: Does your Privacy Policy align with actual data practices federal and state requirements?

Yes.rationale: Aligned privacy policies ensure transparency and regulatory compliance

No or Not sure.rationale: Misaligned policies create significant compliance and legal risks

q18_privacy_policy.helpText: Some states have stricter privacy requirements compared to minimum federal laws. Privacy policies must accurately reflect actual data practices.

rolloverText.Privacy Policy: Legal document describing how an organization collects, uses, stores, and protects personal information, required to match actual practices.

q18_privacy_policy_upload.title: Please upload your privacy policies
q18_privacy_policy_upload.helpText: Upload both internal privacy policies and client-facing privacy documents.

uploaded.rationale: Privacy policy documentation enables compliance verification

q19_external_data_exchange.title: Do you exchange personally identifiable health data with external vendors, partners or systems?

Yes.rationale: External data exchange acknowledged - enables proper third-party risk assessment

No.rationale: No external exchange reduces third-party compliance complexity

q19_external_data_exchange.helpText: External data exchanges include sharing with entities for reimbursement, analytics, or other business purposes.

rolloverText.personally identifiable health data: Health information that can be linked to a specific individual, requiring special protection under HIPAA and other privacy laws.

q20_compliance_environment.title: If these data exchanges are done in a SOC2 or HITRUST-compliant environment, is your system, policies and contracts reflective of these requirements?

Yes.rationale: Compliance framework alignment ensures comprehensive security and privacy protection

No or Not sure.rationale: Framework misalignment creates significant security and compliance gaps

q20_compliance_environment.helpText: SOC2 and HITRUST provide comprehensive frameworks for security, availability, and confidentiality controls.

rolloverText.SOC2: Service Organization Control 2 - auditing standard for security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy of customer data
rolloverText.HITRUST: Health Information Trust Alliance - comprehensive security framework specifically designed for healthcare organizations
rolloverText.TEFCA: Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement - national framework for secure health information exchange

steps.title: Data Interoperability and Standards
steps.description: Comprehensive evaluation of FHIR standards, API requirements, ONC certification, and interoperability compliance
steps.helpText: This section evaluates your system's ability to exchange and use health information across different healthcare organizations, technology platforms, and regulatory frameworks.

q41_interoperability_services.title: Do you provide or plan to provide interoperability services?

Yes.rationale: Providing interoperability services demonstrates commitment to healthcare data exchange

No.rationale: Not providing interoperability services may be appropriate for certain business models

Not sure.rationale: Uncertainty about interoperability services indicates planning gaps

q41_interoperability_services.helpText: Interoperability services enable seamless data exchange between different healthcare systems and organizations.

rolloverText.interoperability services: Technical capabilities that enable different healthcare information systems to connect, exchange, and use data in a coordinated manner across organizational boundaries.

q42_minimum_standards.title: Does the company meet minimum health data interoperability standards, including: FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) v4+, Certified APIs under the ONC Health IT Certification Program if required or Open, standards-based APIs with industry best practices for RESTful APIs and SMART on FHIR where applicable, USCDI (United States Core Data for Interoperability), HIPAA-required technical safeguards (per 45 CFR §164.312) if applicable?
enum: Yes - All minimum standards are implemented, tested and in use
In process, minimum standards are mapped and currently being tested and implemented
In design, minimum standards are designed with plans for testing and implementation in the near future
Not sure what these requires are and no plans to implement them

Yes - All minimum standards are implemen.rationale: Full implementation of minimum standards ensures comprehensive interoperability readiness

In process, minimum standards are mapped.rationale: Implementation in progress shows commitment but creates moderate timeline risk

In design, minimum standards are designe.rationale: Design phase shows planning but lacks implementation validation

Not sure what these requires are and no.rationale: Lack of awareness and planning creates significant interoperability risks

q42_minimum_standards.helpText: These minimum standards ensure your system can effectively exchange health information and comply with federal requirements.

rolloverText.FHIR v4+: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources version 4 or higher - the current standard for healthcare data exchange
rolloverText.ONC Health IT Certification: Certification program ensuring health IT meets federal standards for interoperability and security
rolloverText.USCDI: United States Core Data for Interoperability - standardized set of health data classes and elements
rolloverText.SMART on FHIR: Platform for healthcare apps that provides secure, universal access to health records

q43_data_model.title: Does the company use a proprietary or open data model?

Open standards (FHIR, HL7, OMOP, etc.).rationale: Open standards ensure maximum interoperability and industry compatibility

Proprietary with documented mapping.rationale: Proprietary model with mapping provides some interoperability but limits flexibility

Proprietary, no mapping or documentation.rationale: Undocumented proprietary model creates significant interoperability barriers

q43_data_model.helpText: Open data models facilitate easier integration and data exchange with other healthcare systems.

rolloverText.OMOP: Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership - common data model for observational health data
rolloverText.documented mapping: Clear documentation showing how proprietary data structures correspond to industry standards

q44_analytics_capabilities.title: Does the company offer analytics capabilities on its data model?

Predictive, self-service, structured ana.rationale: Advanced analytics capabilities provide significant value and competitive advantage

Basic reporting only.rationale: Basic reporting provides foundation but limits analytical insights

None or ad hoc.rationale: Lack of structured analytics limits data value and decision-making capabilities

q44_analytics_capabilities.helpText: Analytics capabilities enhance the value of health data by providing insights for clinical and operational decision-making.

rolloverText.predictive analytics: Advanced analytics that use historical data to predict future outcomes and trends
rolloverText.self-service analytics: Tools that allow users to create their own reports and analyses without technical expertise

q45_cots_analytics.title: Does the company use commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) products for analytics?
enum: Widely adopted tools (e.g., Tableau, PowerBI, Snowflake)

Widely adopted tools (e.g., Tableau, Pow.rationale: Widely adopted tools ensure reliability, support, and user familiarity

Mixed custom/COTS stack.rationale: Mixed approach provides flexibility but may create integration complexity

Fully custom, no formal platform.rationale: Fully custom solutions create maintenance burden and limit scalability

q45_cots_analytics.helpText: COTS analytics tools provide proven functionality and reduce development and maintenance costs.

rolloverText.COTS: Commercial Off-The-Shelf - pre-built software products available for purchase and immediate use

q46_cloud_paas.title: Can the data model be instantiated via cloud PaaS (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP)?

Cloud-native design.rationale: Cloud-native design provides scalability, flexibility, and modern architecture benefits

Hybrid model.rationale: Hybrid model provides some flexibility but may limit cloud benefits

On-premises only or unclear.rationale: On-premises only limits scalability and modern deployment options

q46_cloud_paas.helpText: Cloud Platform-as-a-Service capabilities enable scalable, flexible deployment options for healthcare organizations.

rolloverText.PaaS: Platform-as-a-Service - cloud computing model providing a platform for developing, running, and managing applications
rolloverText.cloud-native: Applications designed specifically to run in cloud environments, taking advantage of cloud scalability and resilience

q47_technology_coupling.title: Is the data model tightly coupled to a specific technology stack?
enum: Fully tied to a single tech (e.g., Oracle-only)

Stack-agnostic or decoupled.rationale: Technology independence provides flexibility and reduces vendor lock-in risks

Minor vendor lock-in.rationale: Minor dependencies create some limitations but remain manageable

Fully tied to a single tech (e.g., Oracl.rationale: Single technology dependency creates significant vendor lock-in and flexibility risks

q47_technology_coupling.helpText: Technology independence ensures flexibility in deployment options and reduces vendor dependency risks.

rolloverText.tightly coupled: System components that are highly dependent on each other, making changes difficult
rolloverText.vendor lock-in: Dependence on a single vendor's products, making it difficult to switch to alternatives

q48_model_extensibility.title: Can the data model be easily extended for new use cases?

Modular/extensible architecture.rationale: Modular architecture enables easy adaptation to new requirements and use cases

Extendable with development work.rationale: Extensibility possible but requires development effort and planning

Static or rigid.rationale: Rigid architecture limits adaptability and future growth potential

q48_model_extensibility.helpText: Extensible data models can adapt to evolving healthcare needs and new regulatory requirements.

rolloverText.modular architecture: System design where components can be independently developed, tested, and modified
rolloverText.extensible: Capable of being expanded or modified to accommodate new features or requirements

q49_ai_ml_models.title: Is the product using any AI or ML data models?
enum: Yes, but currently in early testing phase or only available in narrow use

Yes, documented with validation/oversigh.rationale: Documented AI/ML with validation demonstrates mature implementation and oversight

Yes, but currently in early testing phas.rationale: Early-stage AI/ML shows innovation but requires further development and validation

No AI/ML or experimental only.rationale: No AI/ML implementation may limit competitive advantage in modern healthcare

q49_ai_ml_models.helpText: AI and ML capabilities can enhance clinical decision-making and operational efficiency in healthcare systems.

rolloverText.AI/ML validation: Systematic testing and verification of artificial intelligence and machine learning models for accuracy, safety, and effectiveness
rolloverText.oversight: Governance processes ensuring AI/ML models are monitored, maintained, and comply with regulatory requirements

q50_ai_hosting.title: Can the AI models be hosted internally?
enum: Fully deployable in-house or on client infrastructure
Hosted on opaque or third-party vendor site

Fully deployable in-house or on client i.rationale: Internal deployment provides maximum control, security, and data sovereignty

Hosted on proprietary cloud.rationale: Proprietary cloud hosting provides some control but creates vendor dependency

Hosted on opaque or third-party vendor s.rationale: Third-party hosting creates significant control, security, and compliance risks

q50_ai_hosting.helpText: Internal AI model hosting provides greater control over data security and regulatory compliance.

rolloverText.internal hosting: Running AI models on organization's own infrastructure or controlled cloud environment
rolloverText.data sovereignty: Legal concept that data is subject to the laws and governance structures of the country where it is collected or stored

q51_onc_certification_required.title: Will the use of your product require ONC Health IT Certification compliance or compatibility?
enum: Not sure - Continue to next question

Yes - Continue to next question.rationale: ONC certification requirement understood - enables proper compliance planning

No.rationale: No ONC certification required reduces regulatory complexity

Not sure - Continue to next question.rationale: Uncertainty about certification requirements creates moderate compliance risk

q51_onc_certification_required.helpText: ONC Health IT Certification may be required for certain CMS programs and reimbursement requirements.

rolloverText.ONC Health IT Certification: Voluntary certification program ensuring health IT meets federal standards for interoperability, security, and functionality

q52_onc_cms_compliance.title: Is the company compliant with the necessary ONC and CMS interoperability regulations and certification criteria?

Yes, audited or certified.rationale: Audited certification provides highest level of compliance assurance

Self attested or partial certification.rationale: Self-attestation shows compliance awareness and effort

Not sure.rationale: Uncertainty about compliance status creates moderate regulatory risk

q52_onc_cms_compliance.helpText: ONC certification may be required if clients use your system for CMS-based reimbursement programs.

rolloverText.CMS programs: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services quality and reimbursement programs that may require certified health IT

q51_onc_certification_required: Not sure - Continue to next question

q53_ecqms_support.title: Does the technology support required eCQMs?
enum: We need to support this, but we do not yet do so

Yes.rationale: eCQM support enables participation in CMS quality programs

We need to support this, but we do not y.rationale: Missing required eCQM support creates significant program participation barriers

Not Applicable to our company.rationale: eCQMs not applicable reduces compliance requirements

q53_ecqms_support.helpText: Electronic Clinical Quality Measures (eCQMs) are required for various CMS quality reporting programs.

rolloverText.eCQMs: Electronic Clinical Quality Measures - standardized tools for measuring and reporting healthcare quality using electronic health data

q54_fhir_patient_access.title: Are FHIR APIs available for patient access?
enum: Yes, our FHIR APIs are fully live
Not yet, but our FHIR APIs are in development
We need FHIR APIs, but we do not yet begun this endeavor

Yes, our FHIR APIs are fully live.rationale: Live FHIR APIs ensure patient access compliance and modern interoperability

Not yet, but our FHIR APIs are in develo.rationale: FHIR API development shows progress but creates timeline risk

We need FHIR APIs, but we do not yet beg.rationale: No FHIR API development creates significant compliance and interoperability gaps

Not Applicable to our company.rationale: FHIR APIs not required reduces development burden

q54_fhir_patient_access.helpText: FHIR APIs for patient access are required under the 21st Century Cures Act for certain health IT systems.

rolloverText.FHIR APIs: Application Programming Interfaces based on FHIR standards that enable secure access to health information
rolloverText.patient access: Patients' right to access their health information electronically without special effort

q55_adt_notifications.title: Are patient event notifications (ADT messages) supported?
enum: We plan to support this, but do yet do so yet

Yes.rationale: ADT message support enables real-time care coordination and event tracking

We plan to support this, but do yet do s.rationale: Planned ADT support shows awareness but creates current capability gaps

No, not sure.rationale: ADT messages may not be required for all business models

Not Applicable to our company.rationale: ADT notifications not applicable reduces integration complexity

q55_adt_notifications.helpText: ADT (Admission, Discharge, Transfer) messages enable real-time notification of patient events for care coordination.

rolloverText.ADT messages: Admission, Discharge, Transfer messages that notify healthcare systems of patient movement and status changes in real-time

q56_provider_directory.title: Is there a FHIR-based Provider Directory API?

Yes, fully functional.rationale: Functional provider directory API enables comprehensive care network integration

Yes, planned or partially functional.rationale: Partial functionality provides foundation but needs completion

No, not sure.rationale: Provider directory may not be required for all use cases

Not Applicable to our company.rationale: Provider directory not applicable reduces development requirements

q56_provider_directory.helpText: FHIR-based Provider Directory APIs enable standardized access to healthcare provider information.

rolloverText.Provider Directory API: Standardized interface for accessing healthcare provider information including credentials, locations, and services

q57_uscdi_compliance.title: Is the company compliant with USCDI standards?
enum: Yes, partially mapped or committed and mapping is actively underway

Yes, fully mapped.rationale: Full USCDI compliance ensures comprehensive data standardization

Yes, partially mapped or committed and m.rationale: Partial mapping shows progress but needs completion for full compliance

No, not sure.rationale: USCDI compliance may not be required for all business models

Not Applicable to our company.rationale: USCDI not applicable reduces standardization requirements

q57_uscdi_compliance.helpText: USCDI (United States Core Data for Interoperability) defines standardized health data elements for exchange.

rolloverText.USCDI: United States Core Data for Interoperability - standardized set of health data classes and elements that must be supported for certified health IT

q58_prior_auth_apis.title: Is the company compliant with CMS-0057 Final Rule (Prior Auth APIs)?
enum: Not yet, but Prior Authorization APIs are in development

Yes, fully functional.rationale: Prior authorization API compliance streamlines approval processes and reduces administrative burden

Not yet, but Prior Authorization APIs ar.rationale: Development in progress shows compliance awareness but creates timeline risk

No, not sure.rationale: Prior authorization APIs may not be required for all organizations

Not Applicable to our company.rationale: Prior authorization not applicable reduces API development requirements

q58_prior_auth_apis.helpText: CMS-0057 Final Rule requires certain payers to implement prior authorization APIs to streamline approval processes.

rolloverText.CMS-0057 Final Rule: CMS regulation requiring Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and CHIP managed care plans to implement prior authorization APIs
rolloverText.Prior Authorization APIs: Standardized interfaces that enable real-time prior authorization requests and responses

q59_patient_access_rule.title: Is the company compliant with the CMS Patient Access Rule?
enum: Not yet, compliance efforts are currently underway

Yes, fully compliant.rationale: Full compliance with Patient Access Rule ensures patient rights and regulatory adherence

Not yet, compliance efforts are currentl.rationale: Compliance efforts underway show progress but create current regulatory risk

No, not sure.rationale: Patient Access Rule may not apply to all organizations

Not Applicable to our company.rationale: Patient Access Rule not applicable reduces compliance requirements

q59_patient_access_rule.helpText: CMS Patient Access Rule requires certain payers to provide patients with digital access to their health information.

rolloverText.CMS Patient Access Rule: CMS regulation requiring Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, and CHIP managed care plans to provide patients with digital access to their health information through APIs

q60_interoperability_validation.title: Is interoperability audited or attested by a third-party validator?

Yes, fully reviewed externally.rationale: Third-party validation provides independent verification of interoperability capabilities

Only internally validated.rationale: Internal validation provides some assurance but lacks independent verification

No, not sure.rationale: Third-party validation may not be required for all implementations
